name: Lo-ammi
overview: Lo-ammi is a male figure uniquely identified as the son of Gomer, as recorded in Hosea 1:8. There is no tribal affiliation or additional notes provided about him. His role is primarily defined through his relationship to Gomer and the divine naming he received.
namesAndTitles: The name Lo-ammi means 'not my people' and is a proper name given by God, as stated in Hosea 1:9. This name carries significant theological weight, indicating a message from God regarding the identity and status of the people represented by Lo-ammi.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Lo-ammi is the son of Gomer, as noted in Hosea 1:9. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Lo-ammi serves as a symbolic figure in the prophetic message of Hosea, with his name directly reflecting God's declaration about the people. His identity as the son of Gomer and the divine naming 'not my people' highlight a period of judgment and separation between God and Israel. This emphasizes the seriousness of Israel's unfaithfulness and the consequences articulated through Hosea's prophecy.
